title: OpenVidu
description: Self-hosted video conferencing & custom WebRTC: deploy OpenVidu Meet in minutes or build with OpenVidu Platform SDKs.

items.title: Low Latency Live Streaming: WebRTC vs. HLS and DASH (Part 1)
items.content_html: What counts as low latency, why WebRTC hits sub-second delivery where HLS and DASH structurally can't, and where low latency live streaming actually gets used.

items.title: Debugging WebRTC with an AI agent and Grafana MCP
items.content_html: We give a Claude Code agent nothing but read-only Grafana and a broken OpenVidu deployment, then watch it find each root cause in a reproducible case study.

items.title: Deploy OpenVidu on Hetzner Cloud in 15 Minutes
items.content_html: Deploy a self-hosted OpenVidu video conferencing server on a Hetzner Cloud VM with one command, automatic HTTPS and a test bill measured in cents.

items.title: Control your video calls with gestures using free AI
items.content_html: Control your camera, microphone and hand-raise requests with hand gestures, using MediaPipe in the browser, at no cost and without sending video to the cloud.

items.title: Building an AI agent for transcribing and summarizing audio calls
items.content_html: How to build an AI agent that transcribes and summarizes audio calls for your OpenVidu deployment from scratch.

items.title: DynDevice built virtual classrooms with OpenVidu
items.content_html: How DynDevice, the eLearning platform by Mega Italia Media, replaced third-party meeting tools with virtual classrooms built into its LMS using OpenVidu.

items.title: Building a video-enabled CRM with an AI agent
items.content_html: How a complete CRM with embedded video meetings was built with an AI coding agent and OpenVidu Meet, from a single prompt to per-guest room permissions.

items.title: 3 access models for video conferencing apps
items.content_html: The three access models for video conferencing apps compared, anonymous role links, identified guests and registered users, and when to use each.

items.title: OpenVidu 3.8.0 release notes
items.content_html: OpenVidu 3.8.0 is out: user accounts, role-based access and fine-grained room members in Meet, plus a mediasoup overhaul and tighter TURN security.

items.title: Deployment times for WebRTC on five clouds
items.content_html: We deployed the same self-hosted WebRTC platform on AWS, Azure, GCP, Oracle and DigitalOcean, in three architectures each, and timed every single run.

items.title: Host your own private video calls at home
items.content_html: Host a private, free video conferencing server at home on a Raspberry Pi, an old laptop or a mini-PC, with no accounts and no time limits, in three steps.

items.title: 5 conversational AI app ideas for a weekend build
items.content_html: Five conversational AI app ideas you can build this weekend: real-time voice and vision experiments, and the STT-LLM-TTS pipeline behind them.

items.title: OpenVidu Meet vs OpenVidu Platform in 2026
items.content_html: Choosing the right level of abstraction for self-hosted WebRTC in 2026: how OpenVidu Meet and OpenVidu Platform compare, and which one fits your case.

items.title: TURN in production WebRTC: resilience and security
items.content_html: Why TURN is what separates a WebRTC demo from a production deployment: connectivity resilience and security behind NATs, firewalls and mobile gateways.

items.title: How to scale video conferencing architecture
items.content_html: An architecture roadmap for scaling video conferencing from one server to a high-availability system: elastic media plane, HA control plane, autoscaling.

items.title: The scale-in problem in video conferencing
items.content_html: Why you cannot just terminate a media server with meetings running: the scale-in problem, how node draining works, and how OpenVidu solves it.

items.title: 5 React video call platforms compared in 2026
items.content_html: A 2026 comparison of five React video call platforms, Agora, Zoom, Stream, LiveKit and OpenVidu, weighing SaaS convenience against cost and lock-in.

items.title: How client networks affect WebRTC quality and cost
items.content_html: How modern WebRTC connectivity works, and why your clients' networks drive both their user experience and the cost of the servers behind them.
